A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Koala-36M dataset and processing pipeline. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original video-generation evaluations, transition-detection experiments and TSA component ablations, including Tables 2–5.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds predictor comparisons, filtering analyses and generation experiments in supplementary Tables 6–9.

M1.justification: The CSS detector, structured captioner, TSA/WCGB network and AdaLN metric conditioning retain their procedures. Expanded generation-model descriptions and removal of the caption-length rationale do not establish an algorithmic change.

E1.justification: Appendix E adds HD-VG-130M as a training corpus for an evaluated generation model. The existing Panda/Koala coverage, text-to-video task and VBench benchmark remain; resolution and duration extensions concern evaluation settings.

E2.justification: New Table 6 adds Dover as an evaluated TSA comparator and explicitly lists FastVQA, whose scores match v1's dynamic-only ablation. Existing generation, transition-detection and metric-conditioning comparators remain after matching renamed Koala variants.

E3.justification: Appendix E adds FVD evaluation and generation settings of 256 resolution with 4-second duration and 512 resolution with 2-second duration. Appendix D introduces a +10% threshold-perturbation test. The original Table 2 protocol remains unchanged; newly stated training hyperparameters are disclosures.

E4.justification: Appendix D adds targeted analyses of correlations among clarity, motion and aesthetics, and filtering errors as more thresholds are perturbed. Figure 10 replaces the panda example with a tower case. Existing component ablations and the Figure 13 metric-control analysis are retained.

E5.justification: Repeated-run, seed and uncertainty-reporting practices remain unchanged. Both versions retain eight-expert normalization and averaging with the same score-distribution plots. The new correlation analysis reports point estimates without introducing confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables 6–9 substantially extend the reported evidence with Dover results, sub-metric correlations, filtering-error counts and HD-VG/FVD/longer/higher-resolution generation results. For example, Table 8 reports 250K to 340K incorrectly filtered videos out of 48M. Original Tables 2–5 retain their values. New Table 9 reports Koala's 256-resolution, 2-second semantic score as 0.5919, conflicting with 0.5915 retained in Table 2.

T1.justification: Equations 1–4, the transition-rarity assumption and Gaussian 3-sigma detection rule are retained. The added empirical analyses introduce no new formal definitions, derivations, theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: a 36-million-video dataset, detailed captions, improved splitting, suitability-based filtering and metric conditioning. Additional experiments support these existing claims without redefining their scope.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 removes the explanation that longer captions repeat concepts and hinder extraction of key information. The conclusion also drops the explicit statement that performance, generalization and scaling laws need further exploration, while retaining the dataset-size limitation for models above 1B parameters.

D1.justification: Section 5.1 adds transformer-block details, 80GB A100 hardware, batch size 32 and learning rate 0.0001. Appendix B specifies 200K annotated videos where v1 only described a batch. The abstract changes the dataset/code release statement from planned to completed; availability is reported by the PDF, not independently verified.

R1.justification: The cited works and broad research positioning are retained. However, Section 4.2 removes the explicit contrast with MiraData that justified shorter captions, eliminating a specific argument distinguishing this work from that predecessor.

P1.justification: Sentence-level polishing preserves the main narrative and section order. Koala-all becomes Koala-w/o TSA, manual filtering receives clearer naming, and the erroneous Koala-46 reference is corrected. Existing appendix subsections are reorganized under lettered supplementary sections.

P2.justification: The document is comprehensively reformatted from one column to two columns, with the opening figure moved above the abstract and many displays resized or relocated. Tables 6–9 are added. Figures 10 and 14 expand from three to four frames per video, and Figure 10 changes one illustrated prompt.

improvement.justification: The added filtering checks, Dover and HD-VG comparisons, and longer/higher-resolution experiments provide useful corroboration beyond v1. Training and annotation disclosures also improve reproducibility. These gains outweigh the limited losses from removed explanations and the small semantic-score inconsistency between Tables 2 and 9, but do not amount to a substantial overall quality improvement.
